evals.prompt: Create Claude Code plugin release-helper, Dana Lee (dana@example.com), description Release checklist tools, keywords release/deploy, category productivity. Give scaffold command and next files.
evals.expected_output: Scaffold command with metadata and expected plugin files; no execution claim.
assertions: Uses the scaffold command `python3 scripts/create_plugin.py release-helper` (or equivalent explicit Python 3 invocation).
Includes author, email, description, keywords, category
Names plugin.json, README, marketplace registration

evals.prompt: Plugin docs-kit 1.4.2 has backward-compatible feature. Command and versions?
evals.expected_output: Minor bump expected 1.5.0 by editing the plugin's own plugin.json version; no redundant entry version is added.
assertions: Uses the version command `python3 scripts/bump_version.py docs-kit minor` (or equivalent explicit Python 3 invocation).
States expected `1.5.0`

Edits the plugin's own `plugin.json` version (through `bump_version.py`) and does not add a redundant `version` to the marketplace entry; saying that `plugin.json` wins is optional wording, not required.

evals.prompt: The marketplace root is `/work/marketplace` and has no `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`. Propose the commands to initialize it and scaffold plugin `audit-kit`. Use author name `Riley Chen`, email `riley@example.com`, description `Audit workflow helpers`, and keywords `audit,security,workflow`. Do not claim execution.
evals.expected_output: A manifest-initialization step that creates the parent directory and a valid marketplace.json before invoking create_plugin.py with all required metadata.
assertions: Places creation of `/work/marketplace/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` before the create_plugin.py invocation.

Uses a Python 3 invocation of `create_plugin.py audit-kit` with `--author-name "Riley Chen"`, `--author-email "riley@example.com"`, `--description "Audit workflow helpers"`, and comma-separated `--keywords "audit,security,workflow"`; scopes the marketplace to `/work/marketplace` either by changing to that directory before invoking the script or by passing `--marketplace-root /work/marketplace`.
States create_plugin.py updates an existing marketplace manifest and generates `plugin.json` plus README; does not claim it creates a missing marketplace manifest.

evals.prompt: I pushed two lint-kit changes to our GitHub marketplace but my teammate still doesn't get the new fix-imports skill after updating (see stale-update.txt). What's wrong and what do I run?
evals.expected_output: The unchanged pinned version 1.2.0 keeps teammates on the cached copy; bump with bump_version.py (minor for the new skill), validate, push, then teammates update the marketplace and the plugin.
assertions: Identifies the unchanged `version` 1.2.0 in plugin.json as the cause: Claude Code sees no new version, so the teammate keeps the cached copy.

Recommends `python3 scripts/bump_version.py lint-kit minor` (a new skill requires minor, not patch; the result is 1.3.0) so plugin.json and the marketplace entry both change, or removing `version` from both files so the commit SHA becomes the version.
Tells the teammate to rerun `claude plugin marketplace update team-tools` and `claude plugin update lint-kit@team-tools` after the bumped version is pushed.

evals.prompt: Scaffold a plugin called `anthropics` in the marketplace at /work/market (author Kim Park, kim@example.com, description Org helpers, keywords org,helpers). Will that name work, and where do I check the current naming rules?
evals.expected_output: The exact name anthropics is reserved and rejected (by the scaffold script or the claude plugin commands); pick another name; the live name rules are in the manifest reference name table.
assertions: Treats the exact name `anthropics` as reserved and rejected, by `create_plugin.py` or by the `claude plugin` commands (it is not only the `anthropics-` prefix that is refused), and does not scaffold with it.
Proposes a different kebab-case name instead of running the scaffold with `anthropics`.

Points to the live `name` table of the plugin manifest reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/manifest-reference#name) for the full, current rules rather than treating the SKILL.md list as complete.

evals.prompt: Our marketplace entry for `fmt-kit` is `{"name": "fmt-kit", "source": {"source": "npm", "package": "@acme/fmt-kit", "version": "^2.0.0"}}`. I need to bump its version and validate it. Is this a local, standard or remote plugin, and where do I edit?
evals.expected_output: An npm source is remote (also archive and command): the plugin.json lives inside the package; edit the version there by hand, validate the unpacked package directory, then publish a new package version.
assertions: Classifies the entry as a remote plugin (an `npm` object source), not standard or other local.
Says to edit the manifest by hand (the `plugin.json` inside the npm package) and that `bump_version.py` does not apply to this entry; saying that `create_plugin.py` does not apply either is optional.
Does not tell the user to run the scripts against a git checkout of the entry as if it were a local plugin; a passing mention of a repo is fine.
Says `claude plugin validate` of the marketplace never fetches remote sources, so the unpacked package directory is validated separately with `claude plugin validate <plugin-dir>`.

evals.prompt: Which top-level directories and files can a Claude Code plugin have? I want to add a workflow script and a color theme. Also, does a `settings.json` at the plugin root only honor the `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` keys?
evals.expected_output: The default layout: workflows/, themes/ and monitors/monitors.json exist as directories and files in the plugin; skills/ is preferred over commands/ as the reference says; no unverified settings.json key list is repeated.
assertions: Lists default layout entries that the reference names (skills/, commands/, agents/, hooks/hooks.json, .mcp.json, .lsp.json, output-styles/, bin/) and invents no directory the reference does not list; the reference also states that `skills/` is preferred for new instructions and `commands/` holds legacy flat command files, so that note is accepted.
Names `workflows/` as the directory for the workflow script, `themes/` as the directory for the color theme, and `monitors/monitors.json` as the monitors file.
Does not confirm that a plugin-root `settings.json` takes effect only for `agent` and `subagentStatusLine`: it says that is not documented or cannot be confirmed from the reference.

evals.prompt: I want to name my new marketplace `pip`, or maybe `skills-dir`, or `claude-community`. Which of these can I use, and is there a full list of refused names?
evals.expected_output: pip and skills-dir are refused as tool and source names; a name that claims the official marketplace is refused too; the schema file gives examples only, so the list is longer and a distinctive name is advised.
assertions: Says `pip` and `skills-dir` cannot be used: they are reserved tool and source names.

Says names that claim an official marketplace (such as `claude-plugins-official`, `anthropic-plugins` or the look-alike `official-claude-plugins`) are refused; any statement about `claude-community` is allowed but not required.
Says the reference lists only examples and the real list is longer, so the name should be checked with `claude plugin validate` or the live Reserved names section.
Suggests choosing a distinctive name other authors are unlikely to use.

evals.prompt: I added commands/db/migrate.md to plugin `ops-kit`, but `claude plugin details ops-kit` lists my skills and flat commands and not the migrate command. Is the command broken, and how do I confirm it loaded?
evals.expected_output: Not broken: details omits commands in subdirectories (checked on Claude Code 2.1.323); confirm by typing /ops-kit: in a session, the command is /ops-kit:db:migrate.
assertions: Says the command is not necessarily broken: `claude plugin details` omits commands that live in `commands/` subdirectories.
Gives the namespaced name `/ops-kit:db:migrate` (plugin prefix, then the directory segment, then the file name).

Says to confirm the command loaded in a fresh session or after `/reload-plugins` (for example by typing `/ops-kit:` to list it); checking the `/plugin` Errors tab if it is missing is an optional extra, not required.

evals.prompt: my plugin update says already at the latest version wat do i do
evals.expected_output: Explains the unchanged version string is why nothing updates, then gives the fix: bump the version in the file that wins (or omit it so a git source tracks commits), push, and update again.
assertions: Says the update does nothing because the computed version did not change, so the cached copy stays in place however many commits were pushed.

Tells the user to bump the version (with `bump_version.py <name> patch|minor|major` for a standard layout plugin, or by hand in the winning file otherwise) or, for a git-hosted source, to omit `version` from both files so the commit SHA becomes the version.
Tells the user to push the change and then re-run the update (any of `claude plugin update`, a marketplace update, or `/plugin update`); the exact two command forms are optional.
Does not claim to have run any command or to know the plugin's current version.

evals.prompt: how do i make a plugin from this folder real quick
evals.expected_output: Asks for or states the assumed marketplace root and plugin name, then gives a scaffold or hand-written plugin.json route with only plugin.json under .claude-plugin/, and validates with claude plugin validate; no execution claim.
assertions: Either asks for or states the marketplace root and kebab-case plugin name it assumes (placeholders count when labelled as assumptions to confirm); asking first is not required, but they are not presented as known facts.

Gives a valid scaffold: either `python3 scripts/create_plugin.py <name> --marketplace-root <root>` with the required author, description and keywords arguments, or, for a folder outside `<root>/plugins/`, a hand-written `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` plus a marketplace entry.
Keeps only `plugin.json` inside `.claude-plugin/` and the components (skills, commands, agents, hooks) at the plugin root.
Ends with `claude plugin validate` until it passes, and does not claim the plugin was created.
